instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 prohibits any person from engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65, and §13.64(1) requires principals to register, so all paid lobbyists are statutorily required to register/license.

Section 13.63(1)(a) provides the lobbyist license "shall expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year," and §13.64(2) provides the principal registration "shall expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year," making the renewal cycle biennial (24 months).

Section 13.695(2) requires that changes in name of an officer/employee or general area of legislative action disclosed in a filed statement be reported in writing to the board within 10 days of the change; this is the only express change-notification deadline in the bundle.

Sections 13.66 and 13.65 require a lobbyist to be licensed and authorized BEFORE engaging in lobbying on behalf of a principal, so the lobbyist's own registration deadline is prior to (zero days after) initial lobbying activity.

The lobbyist must obtain a separate license under §13.63(1)(a), the principal must file its own registration statement under §13.64(1), and §13.65 requires an additional separate written authorization for each principal-lobbyist pairing — thus separate filings by lobbyist and principal.
Section 13.63(1) lists the contents required for a lobbyist license application (signature, social security number or alternative statement) and does not require submission of a photograph.

Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and employees of the legislature from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695 when acting in an official capacity.

Section 13.621(2) provides that an agency filing a statement under §13.695 and its named officials are not subject to §§13.625, 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, or 13.68 except as provided in §13.695, giving agencies a partial regulatory exemption via the separate, lighter §13.695 reporting regime.
